incidents.name: Microsoft announces removal of Office support for older systems and software versions, July 13, 2026

incident_updates.body: This incident has been resolved.

Microsoft has announced that effective July 13th, 2026, Office applications will no longer be supported on older MacOS and iOS systems, and further, they are removing support for older versions of Office entirely. 
 
	• Clients which are running operating systems earlier than the following minimums will no longer be able to edit or save files after the change: 
		Mac OS – minimum version 12.0 (Monterey) 
		iOS – minimum version 17.0 
 
	• Clients who are using Office 2019 for Mac, regardless of operating system, will be unable to edit or save files after the change. 
	• Clients who are using Office 2021 for Mac or MS 365 apps on iPhone and iPads will continue to function normally, provided the operating systems are supported (as listed above) and at the following minimum software versions: 
		Office 2021 for Mac – minimum version 16.83 
		MS365 apps for iOS – minimum version 2.93 
 
UBC IT strongly recommends that all clients running Office on a Mac, iPhone, or iPad  update their operating systems and Office software before July 13th to prevent any disruptions. 
 
For more information, see https://ubc.service-now.com/kb_view.do?sysparm_article=KB0020043

incidents.name: Canvas Zoom Integration Time Zone Issue

incident_updates.body: This incident has been resolved.

We have identified an issue where Zoom meetings accessed through Canvas may show a start time that is one hour off, even when your Zoom timezone is set to “(GMT-7:00) Vancouver.”

This affects the displayed time only. If your meeting was created using the “(GMT-7:00) Vancouver” timezone, it is still scheduled at the correct time.

Workaround: To see the correct meeting times in Canvas, set your Zoom timezone to “(GMT-7:00) Arizona” when using Zoom through Canvas.

Users accessing Zoom through Canvas may see meeting times shown in the wrong timezone. The timezone may also change on its own when the page is refreshed. We are currently investigating the issue.
In the meantime:
•	When scheduling a new meeting, make sure the timezone is set to “(GMT -7:00) Pacific Time (Vancouver)” before saving.
•	For meetings already scheduled, times in Canvas should display correctly as long as your Zoom timezone is set to “(GMT -7:00) Pacific Time (Vancouver).”

We are currently investigating the time zone issue in Canvas Zoom integration. Users may notice inconsistent time zone displayed on the top of the web page. Please change to “(GMT-7:00) Vancouver” for correct time to join/schedule sessions.

incidents.name: RogersGuest WiFi Network Service Decommissioning November 7, 2026 12:00 PT

incident_updates.body:
On November 7, 2026 at 12:00 PT the RogersGuest WiFi network was turned off at all UBC locations. This includes Vancouver (Point Grey), Robson Square, UBC Okanagan and the remote sites where it was available.

RogersGuest is a legacy hotspot service that Rogers Communications set up for its customers. It is not a UBC wireless service, and UBC and Rogers have agreed it is no longer needed.

Who is affected
Mainly Rogers customers who connect to RogersGuest while at a UBC location. UBC's own wireless networks are not affected (ubcsecure, eduroam, ubcvisitor, ubcprivate, ubcIoT).

What you need to do
If you have been using RogersGuest at UBC, please connect to one of UBC's wireless networks instead:

UBC students, faculty and staff: connect to ubcsecure with your CWL. Setup guides: it.ubc.ca/services/email-voice-internet/wireless-internet-access/wireless-internet-access-setup-documents

Visitors from eduroam member institutions: connect to eduroam with your home institution credentials.

Guests visiting: connect to ubcvisitor.

Need help?

Questions about UBC wireless: UBC IT Service Centre, it.ubc.ca/got-question-about-it-products-and-support

Questions about your Rogers WiFi service: contact Rogers at 1-855-877-WIFI (9434)

incidents.name: Zoom Update Issue on UBC Owned Windows Devices

incident_updates.body: The Zoom Update issue has been resolved. Users who are still experiencing issues should re-install manually by first uninstalling "Zoom and Zoom plug-in for Outlook" through Software Center then re-installing it. A restart may be required before attempting re-install.

A newer version of the "Zoom and Zoom plug-in for Outlook" program has been added to the Software Center which will remediate this issue.
 
Users who are still experiencing the issue of Zoom prompting for administrator credentials should restart their computer. Once restarted, the new version of Zoom should be installed automatically when the computer is next asleep or locked but still connected to the internet.
 
The latest Zoom client could also be installed manually by first uninstalling "Zoom and Zoom plug-in for Outlook" through Software Center then re-installing it.

Some Zoom users on Windows clients may have experienced a problem where Zoom requests to perform an update, but is unable to complete.  This would prevent users from using the Zoom application to attend or schedule Zoom meetings until the update is completed.  

The cause of this issue has been identified and a remediation is in progress of being deployed.  The update will happen automatically and no action should be required of the user.
